chapter: Chicago memories and the road to the Navy
title: Madames' stables of girls and the welcoming committees
summary: Marge explains that in New Orleans and East St. Louis madams brought their girls to dances to meet musicians, later replaced by the young welcoming committees of Basie's day.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: But the musician was always sharp looking. Yes. And another thing, well women nowadays who do hustle and are prostitutes don't have time to hang around any Roseland and any in front of bandstands.
No, no.
They've got to work.
(LAUGHTER).
Yes.

In those days they didn't hustle on the streets. They hustled in houses. You didn't have street walkers, that was their business. And if there was a big band, and like Zutty says, in New Orleans these women that ran these houses, in some big event they'd bring their stable of girls.
Oh I see, you mean....
Sure, they'd bring their, they had a stable of girls. And it was the same way in East St. Louis, the madame......
Bring them to the dance?
Bring them to the dance.
Show them off?
Show them off. That's the only way they met musicians. That's how they met them. But now, shoot, these prostitutes out here, they are too busy working and all that.
And they used to have, girls used to meet when the band would come in on the bus we used to call them, the 'Welcome Committee'.
But that was in the later days, in Count Basie days. But in the early days still had the pimps you know.
Yes, well that's what I'm talking about.
But these welcoming committees really.....
Well really young, bright girls that liked the musicians.

Liked the musicians. In the old days when there were pimps and all, those were the women who worked in those houses. Like you call them call girls now. And they would pick musicians. But the welcoming committee .....
They were young girls.
They followed you from St. Louis
to Kentucky. (LAUGHTER). Little dumb boy, Lord, Old dumby followed Zutty all the way to St. Louis.
Well that is really because, I mean it's obvious that the musician then was like a, I mean he did represent glamour and you know. And up on the stand he was dressed sharper than .....
Like on the Carson show or the Gavett show, they always make cracks about the band you know. Get the girls you know and all. Leave it to the band, they'll tell you who she is. (LAUGHTER).
